summary: The GLC 350e 4MATIC is Mercedes-Benz Australia's first non-AMG plug-in hybrid GLC, and its 25.28kWh usable battery is roughly a third larger than most rivals' — 107km of WLTP electric range is enough that many owners will use the petrol engine only on country trips. Australian reviewers are consistently positive about the calibration and the near-silent EV mode, and note that at $99,900 it undercuts both the GLC 300 petrol it outperforms and the BMW X3 30e. The recurring criticisms are the 2.3-tonne kerb weight, a boot that loses its underfloor storage and spare wheel to the battery, and a five-year service plan that Chasing Cars priced at $7350.
pros: 107km of WLTP electric range from a 25.28kWh usable battery is the longest of any plug-in hybrid SUV under $110,000 in Australia — roughly double the Lexus NX 450h+ (87km) and Volvo XC60 T8, and enough that a typical Melbourne commute never starts the engine

Charges properly for a PHEV: 11kW AC three-phase gets 0-100 per cent in about 2h45m, and it is one of very few plug-in hybrids on sale here with DC fast charging (up to 60kW, 10-80 per cent in about 29 minutes), so a driver without a home charger still has an option

At $99,900 before on-road costs it lists $5200 below the GLC 300 4MATIC petrol it comfortably out-accelerates — 230kW/550Nm combined, 0-100km/h in 6.7 seconds — which is unusual for a plug-in hybrid, and it is 10kW/100Nm up on the $104,800 BMW X3 30e
Braked towing is rated at 2400kg, well ahead of the Kia Sorento PHEV's 1010kg and the Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV's 1600kg, so the battery has not cost it usefulness as a tow car
Mercedes-Benz Australia's five-year, unlimited-kilometre warranty is unconditional and is not tied to servicing inside the dealer network
cons: The 1.2L/100km combined label is meaningless once the battery is flat: Australian testers recorded 7.3L/100km (Chasing Cars), 7.8L/100km (NRMA, CarsGuide) and 8.8L/100km (CarExpert) in charge-sustaining mode on 95 RON premium, so a buyer who cannot charge at home is running a 2.3-tonne petrol SUV and the whole case for the car collapses

The battery sits over the rear axle and takes the boot from the GLC 300's 620 litres to 590, removes the underfloor storage entirely and replaces the spare wheel with a repair kit — the floor is no longer flat

Servicing is expensive even by German standards: Chasing Cars quotes $7350 for a five-year plan on 12-month/25,000km intervals, roughly ten times what a Mitsubishi Outlander PHEV costs to service over the same period

It sits well above both Luxury Car Tax thresholds at $99,900 and above the $75,000 FBT cap, and since the FBT exemption for plug-in hybrids ended on 1 April 2025 there is no novated-lease advantage left to offset that

Kerb weight is about 2316kg — some 200kg more than the GLC 300 — and reviewers note the extra mass in direction changes and under brakes, though the air-free steel-spring suspension copes better than expected
